name: Neil Ferguson
text:
Food Lion has 2 business models. One involves renovated stores with higher-end selections, and commensurate prices, to compete with Harris Teeter, Whole Foods, et al. The other is their traditional model of no frills stores with reasonable selection and lower than average prices. Western Blvd is the latter. I don't need a choice of 6 different Wasabi sauces, or every cut of meat to be "organic," free range, gourmet-corn fed, massaged daily, and read Goodnight, Moon before slaughter. I need cheap prices on groceries. I don't need displays to resemble famous European architecture, or sections floored with Italian marble to suggest Old World open-air markets. I need my staples consistently stocked. This is not a store to compare to high-end stores, and I hope they never fall prey to it. Yes, the parking lot does have wayfarers. Trade offs. No, there are no frills. Perfect.
They have sales often, coupons are abundant, the store is always clean, and the store brands are of excellent quality: just what I need.
I've never had a problem with service, either. I ALWAYS smile, am patient because I can see when they're busy, they are BUSY. I treat every clerk as if if they're me, so I don't hold them to standards of perfection I wouldn't suffer, and understand that they may not feel good that day, or some jerk just made them feel inhuman because of they job they hold. If anyone has a problem with "service," from bitter experience I warn you to check YOUR behavior and treatment of employees: it's most often your behavior that induces bad attitudes and service. Don't be rude, or lordly, or expect of people a standard you'd balk at being held to (perfection). The clerks there smile at me because they remember me, not because they're supposed to. I've even had them open a line up, and come tell me first. Pay off.

text:
I sauntered into Harris Teeter one dreary afternoon with an existential crisis looming over me. With the weight of an impending deadline and a burgeoning case of writer's block, I found solace in the glistening aisles of this seemingly ordinary grocery store. That's where I found him - Samuel. A beacon of hope, adrift in a sea of produce, he was there. When I mentioned my plight, he looked at me with an intensity that could peel an orange, then without a moment's hesitation, he did something extraordinary. He swiftly drew out an avocado from his apron pocket, held it high above his head and proclaimed, "To write, one must live. To live, one must eat. To eat, one must understand the majesty of an avocado." As Samuel sliced open the avocado, he exposed its radiant green heart. This act, curiously, unraveled the tightly wound threads of my literary stagnation.

Fast forward a few weeks, when I found myself wandering the aisles of Harris Teeter again, this time in search of the perfect anniversary gift for my beloved. Distraught over my inability to decide between the artisan cheeses and the top-shelf wines, I bumped into Samuel yet again. He glanced at me and then, as if he could sense my distress, he transformed into a seasoned sommelier and a cheese connoisseur right there in aisle six. His recommendations were flawless. When I revealed the items to my wife, she gasped with delight, convinced that I had finally, after years of clumsy efforts, understood her tastes. She even suggested that we should renew our vows. Thank you, Samuel, you absolute legend, you’ve not only revived my writing career but also breathed new life into my marriage. What more can a man ask for from his local grocer? 10/10 for service.

I love the local Food Lions. Harris Teeter had always been my clear favorite grocery store in NC for most of my life until Food Lion started doing things a bit differently over the past decade. Many of their stores have been renovated recently and some of the more delapidated locations now match the interior quality of the more expensive area chains.

Quality is consistent, their prices are good, and their customer service has never let me down.

The quality of certain products do not match Harris Teeter's, the closest equivalent store in the area, which for certain products doesn't seem worth the slight savings. About once a year, I end up buying a steak from FL instead of HT, out of convenience, and every time, I've regretted it. Comparing the last 5 of each steaks of the same exact cut I that I've gotten from either, I'm still in disbelief that they're somehow the same product, as the FL steaks have had a bad taste every single time while the HT ones were fantastic. At normal prices, the FL cuts come out to a dollar or two cheaper per pound, but the HT ones, while routinely more expensive, routinely go on sale for cheaper than the FL ones, which rarely ever do in comparison. But for something like ground beef where differences in taste are much more difficult to notice, I have no problem stocking up with FL's. The difference is notable in all of the various cuts that I've tried, and buying a NY strip from FL on sale (which run about $10/lb, one of their most expensive) has been a mistake every time, regardless of the location. I don't buy cuts of beef there anymore, but if you don't really care too much, the FL beef is at least acceptable, well handled, and isn't going to make you sick.

Their produce, however, is top quality, and I've never ran into a problem with any of the thousands of produce items that I've gotten, other than some that are unavoidable no matter where you get your food. Their produce prices are routinely great and produce goes on sale frequently.

Frozen foods and dry goods have also been of great quality. The rare couple times that I've ever ran into an issue which was the fault of their distributor and not the store, customer service has offered a refund or replacement every time.

Bakery items are proportional in quality and price compared to more expensive options like HT or Whole Foods. Far cheaper bakery items than the alternative stores, but they are certainly not equivalent products. For example, Food Lion has two main types of chocolate chip cookies that come from their bakery. Their usual tub of their cheap, yet prominently displayed and often on sale CC cookies have filler products and cheap out in areas that make a huge difference, like having high fructose corn syrup and palm oil instead of sugar and butter. But for twice the price, they actually sell decent cookies made with non-disappointing ingredients. Their donuts are absolutely cheap, and absolutely vile, containing chemicals like Propyline Glycol (the base for e-cigarette liquids and "personal lubricants", while not harmful to eat, has no place in food unless you're trying to maximize profits with dirt cheap fillers). Their cakes are not that much better. While cheap and edible, they are disappointing, clearly made with the minimal effort to arrange some disappointing ingredients into the shape of what looks like a cake. However, to get something better from a similar store in the area, you'd have to pay literally almost twice the price. So their baked goods at least have a place amongst people who are trying to diet and don't want their baked desserts to be too alluring, as well with children who both simply won't notice over the predominant taste of sugar. Personally, I really like their "gourmet" cookies of all flavors, but have learned my lesson not to buy their cheapest cookies or any cakes from there again. Not many other places that you're going to find a (small) cake for under $10, though. Their bread is bread, and it's quite great for the price. Hot bar, rotisserie chickens, and deli are good.

text:
Bought a box of Nature's Path Flax Plus Pumpkin Seed cereal in January from the Harris Teeter in Holly Springs. Opened it a couple of days ago and it was completely stale. The box top had a Best By date of  October 2018. So it was out of date long before I purchased it.

I reported the stale purchase to Harris Teeter's corporate office. Store manager Elaine phoned back almost immediately, apologized and offered to replace the cereal when I returned or give me double my money back. Because that store is not near me (I was passing through town when I shopped there) I chose to return the item to a closer store.

I went into Raleigh's Cameron Village Harris Teeter today with the box of stale cereal and my receipt. Manager Marty insisted he couldn't give me what was promised, double my money back. He kept looking at the box, insisting "It's not our product; we don't sell this."

I picked up the phone at the customer service counter, placed a call to the manager of the Holly Springs store and let her talk to Marty. When he put down the phone, Marty instructed the clerk to give me the money and walked away. Marty didn't even have the courtesy to say he was sorry.

I am done with Harris Teeter. Have shopped here for decades, but their product quality, customer service and store atmosphere have precipitously declined since it was purchased by Kroger. I am headed to Publix, maybe even Wegmans when they come to town. Don't have time to pay good money for bad food and bad service.

I packed a duffel bag in my backpack and mounted a @Lime scooter. As I sat at the stop light across from Moore square, responsibly I watched a wayward scootmaster careening through the park with reckless abandon on the same species which carried me. text: I have always loved Publix and I am so excited they have come to North Carolina and are right down the street from me. Out of all the many time I have been there 99 percent of the time it was a great experience and the other 1 percent I spoke to the store manager about in which I explained I don't want anyone fired it was just that an issue made me uncomfortable. He is very polite, listend to my concerns and reassured me he functions on a growth management point of view and focuses on making his employees better, not just chastising (I have had jobs with both types of bosses and bosses like him helped me grow and the others just made me miserable). I see the same employees from when I first started there mixed in with a lot of faces and the vibe is 98 percent welcoming and the other one percent can honestly be chalked up to people under stress with such high demand for everything now a days and dealing with a high influx of people. The other one percent is usually just people getting their feet wet with the Publix way of performing. It's not easy to stay pleasant, helpful and work at 100 percent and they do it very well. As for the store itself. It's Publix, so they have the most beautiful set up of fresh produce, the seafood counter is to die for, everything is always stocked up (honestly I don't know how they are doing it while keeping prices pretty steady) and the deli, well the deli has Boar's Head products and awesome workers. I went to Lidl (4308 Wake Forest Rd. Raleigh, NC 27609) for the very first time yesterday. I was very excited to try shopping there because I’ve heard they have great quality products at low prices. My boyfriend had already eaten dinner and he’s a very squeamish person. Upon discovering that there had been a bug in the bag of cheese, he immediately began to vomit. This really upset me because EVERY dish I made had this cheese in it. So everything I cooked went to waste. Like who wants to see a bug in their food? We dumped the cheese out onto a paper plate to ensure that it was actually a bug. And indeed it was. Not sure what kind, but definitely a bug.

name: Tricia Cotton Dean
text:
As the person who helped Tommy Dean open the very first natural food store in Raleigh (in The Mann-Murr shopping center on Hillsborough Street,) I am still moved to envy all the financially free people who shop at Whole Foods OFTEN and WITHOUT THE SLIGHTEST QUALM. It was when they began serving meat and even introduced products like spam to their shelves that I realized their separate profitability agenda departure from natural, healthy foods.

For ardent people watchers, Whole Foods should be high on their list. It is where wealthy people regularly shop for foods and grocery items. I must vouch for Whole Foods, as they have supremely cornered the market for sourcing excellent foods, products, and service, all which comes at a price, and actually represents a level of Hedonistic self-indulgence that I cannot afford nor even justify.

Aside from wealthy gourmands, it's also a good place to find a lot of wannabe rich people ascribing to a philosophy that IMO, resembles what works for Publix. I have marveled at how Publix has built their Kingdom by shamelessly increasing their prices to around three times what they are sold for by all competitors. Let's call this, "Publix Syndrome." Anyone who has shopped at Publix will get this. I continue to wonder about such a strategy, but the tactic has served them well.

Publix draws a bigger allegiance from shoppers reliant upon food stamps and EBT cards for groceries, But on any given day, people watchers will find a good many shoppers at both the aforementioned stores.

It's their choice, to continue eating, and survive in what could be an unsalvageable economy.

Bottom line?

...When I am convinced that I must have a product so special that it cannot be acquired anywhere than at Whole Foods, and/or nothing but the very best quality/presentation/flavor/and obvious reverence in preparation (like edible Nasturtiums, bakery delicacies, or deliciously rare BeurreKase for some distinctive purpose, people watchers will find me pushing a whole foods cart.

Until I win the lottery or strike it big otherwise, I can be people-watched in the process of regularly procuring groceries from Harris Teeter and Food Lion.

Name: 16_raleigh_store raleigh_best_grocery
name: Rodger
text:
When we moved to Raleigh in 2004 (yes, you can laugh, from the Bay Area) this was an above-average store to buy healthy food with some items even having a history/audit trail (where the food comes from, who has handled it and how, practices and methods used, etc.). Prices were high, yes, but the quality of both food and service were noticeably good. We’re not wealthy but are in a good enough place that we can pay a little extra for better quality.

Unfortunately, since Amazon gobbled them up, things have noticeably gone down hill. Amazon’s insane focus on ultra lean operations, including the lowest possible labor cost and, all that and more, at very thin margins, has allowed mediocrity to creep in.

Staff: still pretty friendly but a number of weird mistakes made we personally experienced and, at least perceptually, less genuine customer care.
Selection: significantly gone down; granted, the pandemic has hugely impacted everyone and the supply chains are still shadows of what they were before.
Food Quality: seems they’ll offer it if they can buy it, but overall freshness and quality have definitely suffered.

Also, for some reason, we can’’t figure this out at all, we run into many pricing mistakes in our disfavor. Almost every time we shop, there is something on the receipt where we were overcharged, and sometimes by more than 100%. Thus, now each visit, before we leave the store, we go through the receipt line by line to make sure we didn’t pay $5 or more too much. In one instance the delta was around $20, which is real money.

You might ask, why do we still buy there? For us, at least, there aren’t any credible alternatives. You say, “farmer’s markets have fresh produce.” True, but we don’t know any that sell organic produce. I’d love supporting local farmers, but many forcibly run at razor thin margins and seem to either not want to or cannot afford to switch to farming practices that don’t include pesticides and other scary chemicals.

What our local farmer’s market does offer is two livestock farmers that offer humanely raised and slaughtered meat. More expensive, yes, but if you know how factory farming works and have spent even just moments at a slaughter house then you hopefully would agree you cannot morally justify buying any meat that’s not humanely raised and slaughtered. So there you have it. Next up, family vacation pics…

text: Whole Foods? Yes. Whole Produce? No! The day I went to this Whole Foods store (one of three capturing this market on the north end of Raleigh - the other two being Trader Joes and Earth Fare) all of the leaf produce was shoved into one corner of one refrig unit on the side. They had mounds of potatoes, apples and tons of citrus in piles but the celery was pre-stripped, the spinach was in terrible shape and the choice of onion was limited to two kinds. I've seen better produce at Food Lion and a minor store at that. Getting past the disappointing produce, one encounters fish (good selection, looked very fresh but extremely pricey), then meat in two sections (deli is next to bakery on the opposite side) - prepackaged chicken (marked $6 and higher per package), and the beef - again beautifully displayed but very pricey (ground beef at $7.99/lb, for real?). The 365 brand is their generic and its quality is good, so I would recommend you buy and try that brand first if you are looking at price/quality. The lunch layout is organized. The cheese counter is the best next to Earth Fare's cheese counter. The deli is ok but nothing compared to Harris Teeter's two north end stores. The bakery, on the other hand, is the shining star to this store and should be featured on the news. The cakes and other baked goods on display are the finest I've seen anywhere in Raleigh except for specialty bakeries and by far beat any grocery store chain. The parking at this store location is screwy as you have to make two sharp turns off the main road for entry. The store is very clean. The employees helpful. But like all Whole Foods stores, be prepared to part with your whole paycheck as I found zero bargains the day I was there. Nothing and I mean nothing was marked down or on sale (unlike Trader Joes and Earth Fare who offer sale items throughout the store). Go for the baked goods, but be prepared to pay through the nose for huge meat and seafood departments.

text: Very disappointed in my recent experiences with multiple Harris Teeters. It seems the illusion of a full stock takes precedence over accurate product (price tag) labeling. After having just purchased a similar looking but very unsimilar tasting green (and ruining the whole recipe) at this Harris Teeter, which had been intentionally placed there incorrectly by the produce staff to fill the empty spot when they didn't receive the actual item on the last shipment and didn't even bother to change the price tag label to reflect the layout modification, I was very frustrated with this location and refused to go back. I decided to try the new Harris Teeter store at Brier Creek instead in hopes that they valued accuracy more than their appearances (or, since they were new, perhaps wouldn't feel pressured to fake looking better) but found the same case there as well. Rather than trusting their signage this time, I had the manager on duty paged to confirm my suspicion that the same poor company practice of intentional consumer deception was being committed there also. As a consumer, I rely on produce signs/labels to choose the right item when many of the greens look very similar and have no markings on the individual bunches. If a product is mislabeled as another similar-looking item, and the individual product has no tag or number codes to differentiate it, how is the consumer ever supposed to trust that they're buying the right thing? Only by relying on the price tag label. So when this system is regularly and intentionally manipulated at corporate's demand in an attempt to make the store "look fully stocked", the customers are the ones who are manipulated and hurt by the result of these mindless corporate decisions. Once again, another prime example of corporate idiocy that cares more about its looks that its functionality for the consumer. The manager on duty was both powerless to change the store's corporate mandate to partake in this fraudulent practice and apathetic to the negative effect it has on his customers. If I can't trust that I'm buying the right thing, I simply won't be a customer anymore. I'll take my family of seven's business somewhere that respects my time and money and doesn't play manipulative, petty games about the illusion of stock. I'd much rather see a few holes of missing items, which is completely normal, than to have to wonder every time if I'm wasting my hard earned money on the wrong item. Until corporate sees the flaw in this appearances-over-functionality mandate, replaces it from the top down with a consumer-focused alternative, and personally apologizes, I will go out of my way not to shop at Harris Teeter ever again, and I'd advise you all to do the same.

Here are 2 quick highlights from my visit here today (unfortunately I didn’t have the time to drive to Cary or the Whole Foods on North six Forks, which I much prefer when I’m able) -

There are only two minor reasons I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 stars.

First, as everyone surely knows prices are on the higher side here. Truth be told, I don't mind paying a premium for prepared foods, charcuterie platters, etc. However, they also have products like Wegman's brand dry pasta noodles selling for $5/bag when you can buy the same exact item at almost any other grocery store for $1-2/bag. Not a huge deal, I can buy noodles elsewhere - but it does mean that I need to remain somewhat diligent while shopping at Wegmans, in order to avoid mindlessly grabbing things like the noodles and significantly overpaying.

Second, my wife and I have run into stock issues more than once at this location. While this isn't necessarily Wegmans fault (the last time, they said their supplier shipment just hadn't come in as expected), it's something that I generally don't expect to encounter as often at a higher-end grocery store.

text:
Since I wrote the review below, my thoughts about Wegmans have changed. On the plus side, they've eliminated plastic bags and charge for paper ones and I'm seeing more reusable bags YAY.

Other than that, they've gotten really annoying and I go less often:

Too often when I go, there are few leafy greens on the shelves. Do they continually order too few or just not restock as needed?

For some products, the Wegmans brand is the only option, even where there's a standard everyone expects.

The latest is that you can only turn in 2 SodaStream canisters per visit, even if you've buying 5 full ones. Why?? They seem to go out of their way to be annoying.

Heads up: if you don't enter your phone number at checkout (so that they can sell your purchase history to a broker) you can't return even a Wegmans brand product unless you kept your receipt. The can't or won't verify purchase by credit card. Don't give stores your info, just keep receipts.

----
Wegmans is MILES better than Harris Teeter, the main local competitor.

The produce is usually good quality, and more reasonably priced, but it's often odd what they don't have. It's October and no Brussels sprouts?

Many of their store brand products are good, but it's a hassle that they don't often offer alternatives. The canned beans, for example, are just okay, so that's a trip to another store.

They have a great wine selection, and their prices are much better than other groceries and wine shops.

New Comment AUG 2 2035
Publix sushi is the best grocery store sushi!  The Hawaiian Roll Salmon (10-piece for $10.99) is incredibly delicious and worth every penny! It has nice chunks of fresh avocado and silky salmon sitting on top of imitation crab uramaki, all drizzled with a creamy, mildly spicy sauce—and tiny pops of roe add a fun burst of texture. Absolutely scrumptious! I enjoy it in my car while watching planes take off or land from the nearby airport—such a relaxing and quick break!

New comment APR 26 2025
I’m co-hosting a baby shower and at 6pm the night before I realized I didn’t have the sheet cake ordered!  I called and spoke with a delightfully positive, Jakiya, in the bakery who listened, and said there are full sheet cakes I can choose from in the refrigerator case, and definitely they can write congratulations to the mom and dad on it.  Jakiya said she would be there when I wanted to come in first thing.  I was happy to meet her, and yes, she was as delightfully positive in person as she was on the phone!  She helped me pick out the perfect cake and worked with the talented lady who did the writing to be sure it was the light blue I wanted.  Such a perfect encounter!  Thanks, Jakiya and Publix!

New comment JAN 2025
There are more reasons to praise the employees at Publix.  I went in to get bok choy for a recipe, and had no idea what it looked like.  An employee, Ward, in the produce department was busy loading fruit onto the table display, but he was smiling and helpful when I asked for help and led the way to the section with the bok choy.  He was extremely knowledgeable about the produce and continued to be super nice, smilingly helping me.  I also picked up some of the $5 sushi they have on Wednesday.  Yum!  Then I decided to use a lane with a cashier since instead of self-checkout since I had the bok choy and no idea how to check it out myself.  The cashier, Zobon, was upbeat and knew what to do with the bok choy, and he also automatically gave me the senior discount, which I appreciated, otherwise I would have forgotten.  Zobon made the checkout pleasant.  On the way out, I stopped an employee, Alissa, who was pushing a long line of carts to ask a question about something I wondered about inside.  She was OK with being stopped to answer my question and smilingly responded.  Everyone is so kind.   It is clear that management hires great people with good attitudes, and I see it every time I'm in the Leesville store.  Thank you!

New comment SEP 2024:
I dropped in for one item and was ringing it up at the self-checkout that I KNOW requires a credit/debit card.  I opened my wallet and my card  wasn’t there (I had been paying bills and mistakenly left it on my desk).  I dreaded telling the employee managing the self-checkout area.  I don’t know if readers of this review are too young to remember the movie, “You’ve Got Mail.” But I remember Meg Ryan gets in the credit-card only line and she doesn’t have a card.  The people in the line behind her and the cashier are seriously judgmental and nag her relentlessly about her mistake.  That’s what I expected, but the guy managing the self-check out area (Zach) didn’t frown or make me feel badly, he was pleasant, asked if I had Apple Pay and offered to help me use the iPhone app (I didn’t have set up on my phone), then he asked if I had cash, yes I did, and he said, “No problem.”  He pressed buttons to get a slip of paper about my purchase and said pleasantly, “Come with me” and walked me over to the customer service counter, I said a big thanks, and the guy there rang up the sale.  I appreciate Zach’s wonderful customer service and imagine he’ll do well in whatever is ahead of him in his career.  Thanks to Publix for creating a great environment for customers.

The bakery is marvelous!  Tons of choices, and specialty cake/pie slices for two people.  Yum!  Customer service is always excellent throughout the store.

I’m officially renaming this place “Publix Chick-fil-A Junior.”
This is only my fourth time shopping here—since it’s a little further than my usual store—but every single visit has been marked by exceptional customer service, friendly smiles, and warm greetings from every employee I encounter.

Two visits in particular really stood out.
Once, I walked in literally one minute before closing. Instead of being rushed or turned away (which has happened to me at other stores), the manager met me at the door with a kind attitude, encouraged me to come in, and even welcomed three other people who pulled up right after me. No pressure, no attitude—just hospitality.

And today? I came in with my three kids, and again, the service was top-tier. A gentleman named Carter didn’t just ask if I needed help getting my bags to the car—he kindly insisted, like the team always does, and made the kids laugh the whole way there. Another associate, Katherine, gave the kids stickers. ease.

These small, thoughtful acts of kindness mean the world to busy parents like me.
10 stars for the store.
10 stars for the team.
And 100 stars for Carter and Katherine!

text:
Not the shining examples Food Lion corporate offices undoubtedly hoped for.  It's a grocery store that's reasonably well stocked (although the meat section leaves a LOT to be desired) and reasonably clean.  What earns this place the 3 star review is the people.  Yes, I know working at Food Lion is not the peak career most people working there hope for.  That doesn't mean they shouldn't strive to do a good job.  The attitude of the people working here (in general...I'm sure there are a few stars in the darkness) is apathy.  They don't seem to care.  I asked one person stocking the shelves for help finding the "international foods" section and got, "I dunno" in response.  No attempt to find out.  Just "I dunno" and back to stocking the shelves.

The meat counter (I refuse to call them butchers because they're not even close to being real butchers) is just as apathetic.  Ask for a special cut and you'll be treated to an attitude of near disbelief that you'd impose on their time, then you'll get a flat refusal because "we don't do that" (this in response to a request of a 4lb chuck roast).

The check out lines are populated with people who seem to be working on autopilot.  They do their jobs, but their disposition is far from sunny.  I don't believe I've ever received "service with a smile"...hell, I don't think I've ever been told "have a nice day" either.  Saying "hello" to them seems to be wasted breath because, in the rare occasions where "hello" is even acknowledged, the reply is flat and automated.

Yesterday, when I got to the checkout with my single 12-pack of beer, the person at the register was having a conversation with another employee who was leaning on the counter about 6" from the credit card scanner (you know, where most people stand to pay and pick up their groceries).  After continuing their conversation for a good 30 seconds, I started to walk to another register when the person at the register picks up my beer and scans it....not a word of hello or apology...just scans it like I had just arrived.  The employee leaning on the counter just stayed there, looking through her phone.  The person at the register told me the total and went back to chatting with the employee at the counter, leaving me to wonder if I should ask the employee to move or what.  Ultimately, I had to turn the credit card machine as far as it would go towards me (which still put me standing 6" from the employee at the counter) to use my card.  Once the transaction was done, the person at the checkout slid my beer to where most people would pick up their groceries...directly in front of the person standing at the counter.  I had to walk around to the other side to pick it up!

The examples above are all examples of the service you'll get here.  You can get your groceries and get em home.  The place is reasonably clean and well stocked.  Just don't expect the employees there to give a damn about your experience.  Whenever possible, I go to another grocery store to get my groceries. The fact this place is about a mile from my home means I'm here often, but I make sure to adjust my expectations before I walk in, because I know they're gonna be apathetic and/or blatantly rude.

text:
The entire experience was what one might compare to shopping at a grocery store.

The isles contained a variety of well organized foods and goods that lined up precisely with the signage above.

I came specifically looking for juice, and as expected this could be found directly under the "juice" section, though inconveniently it was at the opposite end of the isle I started at.

I was also able to acquire chips from the chips section, and dip nearby. A very sensible placement and I commend the store on this decision.

All of this leads to the unfortunate end of my review wherein I must lambast the experience.

Checking out was a trying experience wherein no less than two of the items my friend was purchasing did not scan or ring up properly. Frustrated, overwhelmed, and fussy like a baby, he proceeded to ask for the assistance of store employees. Two responded (a little bit of wasted labor, but I personally appreciated the solidarity), and were able to solve the issue at hand. My friend then sheepishly attempted to cope with the embarrassing situation through a comment designed to make light of the situation. A "dad joke" about getting the offending watermelon for free.

To my horror and absolute dismay I watched powerless as they sarcastically disparaged his joke. He, on the verge of childlike tears, choked back a sob. The shock prevented me from intervention, and we were forced to finish the shopping experience in quiet mourning for his dignity.

Four out of five stars. I won't be back, because I don't live here. But he will be.

I prefer this layout (similar to Lidl's and I prefer Aldi to Lidl: YMMV). Personnel are different and a few prices. All locations follow ALDI guidelines.

I don't like tons of choices when shopping !  Aldi has it's own branded products (made by the name brand people; ask Aldi online and they will let you know who supplies them, item by item). Aldi generally has one of each kind of item. Not 6 sizes of same item & not 16 manufacturers of each item. You want tomato soup, you get the item label & they sometimes have two types of that item. Cat food 4 flavors of canned cat food. Nice & simple. I hear the meats are great; I wouldn't know anything about that. I hear in Germany (Aldi & Lidl are German companies & very popular throughout Europe (better meat and bakeries there) ;)
Aldi meets my needs for most of my grocery needs and on occasion, I have picked up something from their (not so grocery oriented & limited item exposure) specials aisle.
I am one of those people that isn't so status quo (a bit Asperger'd) and a lot Vegan-ized. I like produce, a little skim milk (They have wide range of healthy choices) and salmon each day. In these areas, Aldi suffices for me.
If you are status quo and love loads of sizes and brands, Aldi just isn't for you; however, you could still find some items that will keep a few bucks in your bank, where they belong.
March 12, 2019: Two lb frozen salmon fillets (skin on, boneless) individually wrapped (3 to 6 oz ea) sale $4.59 usually $5.95. Skim milk gallon $1.80 (give or take a couple of cents).
Stop in and try them ;)
YMMV

text: On October 21, 2020, I shopped at the Sprouts in Raleigh, store # 540. Though I live a distance, pre-pandemic, I would shop at Sprouts on a regular basis. text:
If you are familiar with the Whole Foods brand then Wegmans is on the next level up. In fact, the quality of goods on the shelves, the R2E (Ready to Eat) areas and even the coffee bar are set on a higher scale that WFs. However be warned!! That ain't your grandmom's budget friendly grocery. No way!! You don't come here cash unless you got the truck with the guard riding too.

This is a BYPC (Bring Your Platinum Card)  kinda store!

Out Front: No matter where you park in the lot you are made to believe you're only a few feet from the door. The lot is super clean and most importantly, IT IS WELL LIT! There are cameras that catch you  coming and going and from every angle. SECURITY!!!

Entrance: Carts greet you at the door as well as a variety of QGs (Quick Grags) to get your shopping experience started. Smell that Java?!? Yes you know you do. It is the first aroma that breaks through you nose as you round the first turn into the main run way. Hold up, gotta take a sip of this fresh brewed Columbian. Hummm... Did I Say FRESH BREWED! MoMA! Come get me!

In to the fresh meat section. There is no "green slime" in here. The steaks look ready to grill and the chickens are laying around with their heads cut off just waiting to be based and broiled. What the cluck?!? Is that sushi? Ahh man it is on! Hey, you better get here soon for real!

There are about 5 R2E stations here with a wide variety of eateries. There is something for everyone. I talk about the meat factor but veggies and vegans this is your stop too. You never have to see a meat product if you don't want to because this place is big enough to hide everything in plain sight.

Service: Folks this is a grocery, convenience, deli, pizza, inside garden, better than starbucky coffee shop, department store. Ok, they sell everything except tires folks. The humongous plus that Wegmans has is the staff. I'm not just saying that either. Test it I did. I asked a staffer who was putting some stuff on a shelf if they had those really thin ginger snap cookies. This dude stop what he was doing and walked me four isle and on race track over and held up a box and said, "Are these the ones you like"? REALY!!!!! Who does that? I thought this was a fluke or one employee just trying to break away from his mild manners job just to show his super knowledge if the store. So, yep as soon as he walk away. I put the cookies back and went to the far side of the store and found another staffer. I made the same request and you are not gonna believe this but this person did the same exact thing! I didn't put them back this time

Recommendations: I was most impressed with the fact that as you leave one area and move to another on you don't find lingering aromas. The coffee doesn't bleed over into other areas and the same for the other areas. You smell apples with apples and oranges with oranges but not the two together.

The only  reason I gave them 4 stars is because if the price. I had to spend part of my mortgage money and all of my vacation money for the things I bought. I suggest you come here at least once so make it on the day you know that you really deserve to have true goodness in your life. Or, if you are so sad that you forgot what happiness looks like. There are staff here who work the checkout areas just to make your day happier and forget you just dropped a car note on goods.

text: Prices at Aldi on some items are better compared to other grocery stores, but after extensive price-shopping, for the items I regularly purchase, it evens out in the end when I compare them to Foodlion. I get it that they don't bag your groceries, but heaven forbid you bring a self-standing tote & place it inside the shopping cart for them to place your items inside. I mean, they're going to place them inside the cart anyway, why not just place them inside the stand up tote?? The young black girl checking me out earlier this week was horribly rude when I asked if she could do that versus combining the items in my cart with the lady's groceries who was checking out behind me. text:
The produce is good quality, on par with but no better than Kroger. Tiny little meat section crammed in the back corner; rather pricey but seems to be fresher than most places. They do have fresh lamb chops and cutlets, which is a pretty rare thing.

Very disappointed with their 'bulk spices'. Consists of two end row displays, only one of which was 'bulk' and that one had very limited variety. The non-bulk spices were quite reasonably priced but again limited variety.

There is a quite impressive selection of bulk nuts and seeds right in the middle of the store. Similarly impressive coffee bean and tea selection. Lots of organic/vegan/gluten free options in the snack/baking area. Great selection of honeys and syrup too.

Overall it is a pretty nice store, although definitely not up to the hype swirling around when it opened. Recommend it if you specifically want the organic, vegan, etc. options or slightly more specialty items. Doesn't really mesh with my own needs though so I probably won't be back.

Once again, another prime example of corporate idiocy that cares more about its looks that its functionality for the consumer. The manager on duty was both powerless to change the store's corporate mandate to partake in this fraudulent practice and apathetic to the negative effect it has on his customers. If I can't trust that I'm buying the right thing, I simply won't be a customer anymore. I'll take my family of seven's business somewhere that respects my time and money and doesn't play manipulative, petty games about the illusion of stock. I'd much rather see a few holes of missing items, which is completely normal, than to have to wonder every time if I'm wasting my hard earned money on the wrong item. Until corporate sees the flaw in this appearances-over-functionality mandate, replaces it from the top down with a consumer-focused alternative, and personally apologizes, I will go out of my way not to shop at Harris Teeter ever again, and I'd advise you all to do the same.

name: Juliette “Jette” Rouse
text:
Today was my first experience at a Wegman's, and I must say for such an "upscale" grocery store I was sorely disappointed!

My first impression upon entering the store was: Chaos! The entryway dumps immediately into the produce area in such a way that every person who enters or exits the store must walk THROUGH the first section of produce. This makes for a very crowded walkway that discourages leisurely browsing.

I found the layout of the store confusing and difficult to navigate, so I pulled out my phone and went to the Wegmans.com website in the hopes it could help me locate the products I needed. Unfortunately every single item I searched listed an incorrect aisle, so I had to hunt down an employee to help me. Finding an employee proved equally difficult since there appeared to be no standard uniform. Every employee I saw during my shopping trip was wearing a different colored shirt, and only a few wore name tags.

The employee I flagged down was perplexed by the incorrect results I was getting on the website and suggested I download the app instead. While this did solve the problem, it is an extra step I shouldn't have to go through, especially for a store I might never visit again.

As far as the inventory goes, this was also rather disappointing. Several of the produce items I examined were already going bad. Many of the brand names of packaged products I typically purchase were unavailable, and they seemed to be trying to force customers to use their Wegman's store brand instead.

I finally got through my list as best I could and proceeded to the checkout where I would be met with yet more disappointment. Being a first time customer, I of course did not have a loyalty card yet. Every other grocery store I've ever shopped at, the cashier has had a card to swipe for customers without one, or at the very least can provide customers with a new one and the accompanying paperwork. But no, instead I was informed that I would have to visit customer service on my way out to fill out an application, and they could then refund me the difference for any sale items I might have purchased.

Next, an item would not scan due to a worn barcode tag. The cashier called a manager over, who could not find the item (a bag of Wegman's brand clementine oranges) on the app and said she would have to go find another package to scan. But the impatient cashier was not willing to wait and instead told me I could go to customer service on my way out and purchase the item there... As if her time was more valuable than mine!

Needless to say, I will not be going back to this store!

text:
There's no place like Wegmans! You have to see it to believe it. Shopping for groceries shouldn't be boring or a drag to do because we have to shop quite often! From the moment you walk in, you're right in front of the colorful, very organized & freshest produce section ever! The sky light is a nice touch. There are details about the store that you can't ignore and make the experience that much nicer. Everyone is so delightful and nice, they are helpful and knowledgeable of their products! Even if you run into a worker who may be outside of the area they work in, they still help! It's amazing. They also have ready to eat, made fresh daily, packaged meals. Chefs are on staff with their team and they're all so helpful. Have a question about how to cook your dinner tonight? They will tell you! There are lots of perks as a customer to make it easier and convenient to shop here. Their app for discounts, called the "shoppers club", you can find in the app store [wegmans].
Sign up and use your phone number at checkout. Boom, save money.
If you know what you need and want to be in and out as easy as possible then get the [wegmans scan] app. Bring your own bags! I know you got them in the car, grab em! Open them up on your cart, use your phone to scan each item and bag as you shop. No need to unload your cart 3x!
To pay, you use the self checkout lane. The scan app bar-code is on the screen, ready to itemize your order. Pay and save time.
Obviously, my favorite.
Meals2Go is another goodie for the hungry on the go!
Pre order from your phone from any of the cafe shops for lunch&dinner. Use carryout, curbside or delivery. Another time saver. So back to the point, it's a pretty awesome place to call your local grocer. They got you! I'm a Florida girl who grew up on Publix, never heard of a Wegmans. I get it now haha! Don't get me wrong, Publix is still a pleasure but competition is good for us! Look them up and better yet,  go hungry and shop!

At Wegmans I found I actually had options and could select from a number of amazing Empire Kosher products ranging from whole chickens to hot dogs to cold cuts.

Beyond that however, I've also never seen such an abundance of plant-based protein products carried in a store from all the major brands (mainly Impossible and Beyond meats). If you have any sort of dietary restrictions and have trouble finding things at the grocery store, this is for sure a place you're going to want to check out.

(p.s - for anyone with a sweet tooth I HIGHLY recommend trying their canolis)

text:
I'm from Texas, the land of HEB, Central Market and Whole Foods, so I'm very particular about grocery stores...(actually, I'm particular about everything, but that's a different story)...my verdict: Wegman's is a little overhyped.  However, it is the best grocery store option in the area.

The good:
- a great produce section with wide variety, really fresh fruits produce and low prices
- the deli has an awesome selection of meats and cheeses
- the bakery is stocked with delicious and fun desserts and great fresh bread
- the seafood case, although limited, has great choices and prices
- lots and lots of prepared foods that you just have to heat and eat or cook with little effort
- the frozen and shelf stable section is huge and has pretty much everything you need

The not-so-good:
- No sales and limited coupons.  Yes, they have low prices, but Harris Teeter and Whole Foods sometimes beat their prices with sales, member specials and coupons.  The only coupons Wegmans offers if on its generic brand.
- I wish more of the meat was in the meat case instead of prepackaged.  They only have higher end meat in the case, everything else is prepackaged.  I prefer to get my ground beef and chicken breast from a case.
- The "Asian" section doesn't have anything South Asian.  As a Pakistani, this is very frustrating...(the section does have a selection fo things from East Asia)
- They tend to run out of things like certain prepackaged salads, sauces, etc
- They don't have any good quinoa options - just a low end boil-in-a-bag brand and a high end heirloom style.  Butter options aren't great either
- They got rid of their whole wheat sourdough bread...booooo!

Stroller Status: If you go at an off peak time, there's tons of space for your stroller.  It's a little trickier to navigate at busy times, like Sundays

Wegmans is an amazing place. The various departments are well-stocked, and the opportunities to purchase whole meals for eating in their nice dining area make it possible to turn grocery shopping into a leisurely, enjoyable--and tasty--experience.

But it may not be for everyone. For example, if you're a name-brand shopper, you're likely going to be disappointed at Wegmans, as they heavily leverage their store brand products in just about every department.

Even so, such people may still find Wegmans worth a visit. Wine aficionados definitely should go, as their wine section is impressively well stocked--and at all price ranges, too. The deli and cheese departments are also enticing.

I LOVE WEGMANS! Seriously, I can't say enough good things about Wegmans. Their staff, the selection, the atmosphere..everything is all amazing!
I go weekly either on Tuesday or Wednesday and the crowd has died down a bit since the first two weeks of it opening. I love that there are always Wegmans associates nearby if you should have any questions. The items you are looking for are normally always in stock with a great variety. Their prices are very competitive and beat a lot of the other stores nearby.

Pros:
Accept coupons PLUS doubles coupons .99c and under.
Produce selection is huge and all ready to eat! (no moldy or expired fruits/veggies like other stores leave out)
The 'Wegmans' brand is actually a very good brand and I have tried dozens of items without one complaint.
Beautiful flower assortment at great prices.
One stop shop: groceries, coffee place, multiple places to eat, to-go food, plus different "markets" like cheese, bakery, fish etc!
Tons of parking upstairs AND downstairs with the cart escalator
Good amount of self checkout if you are in a rush
Great beer/wine selection

Cons:
The only con I could think of and I had to dig deep for this....they do not offer as many weekly/monthly store coupons (paper or digital) as other grocery stores in the area do.

name: Gail Showers
text:
Having grown up in WNY I was accustomed to Wegmans and loved to shop there. When we made the move to Cary, NC 20 years ago I was so disappointed with the grocery stores.
Well, today was amazing!! Finally we have Wegmans! Bye, bye Food Lion and Harris Teeter....Wegmans is here! This store was just everything a grocery store should be...and the customer service was incredible. I spoke with staff from meat, bulk, wine, bakery, grocery,and dairy and unlike the HT close to my home, nobody had to call someone to get an answer! Each member was able to answer my questions and requests to help me find all my favorite items. We filled two carts and we will make this our weekly shopping spot (well...until they open in Cary). The bakery clerk even explained that if I wanted the pepperoni and cheese bread (they carry around certain times) that I could call a few days ahead and they would make some for me! The bulk clerk told me the date sponge candy would arrive. The butcher showed us right to the Wegmans brand Italian sausage. The wine clerk walked us over to the infused oils halfway across the store and made us feel like we were the only ones there....even as thousands of people were there. A grocery clerk I asked to point me to where Chavettas marinade was walked right to the spot and pulled a bottle from the shelf as if he’d always worked there. At checkout....even with the store being that busy, I only waited about five minutes. The ONLY disappointment was that they were out of Bison Dip. The dairy clerk said they had ordered three times the corporate suggested amount and had run out in the first hour....and then he was so well informed he told me about the next two shipments and when they would arrive. You can’t get that at HT and Food Lion 😎 Welcome Wegmans!! I have missed you. 😍
Some misinformed guy said Wegmans was NY prices...if a gallon of milk is $1.74 ($2.99 @ HT), 90/10 ground beef is $2.99 ($5.99 @HT), Red Oak is $17.99 ($21.99 @HT) I’ll take those NY prices all day. Essentially, for Southern folks...imagine Wegmans as regular everyday grocery prices cheaper than Food Lion in the middle...then add a Whole Foods specialty area, Cheaper than Total Wine HUGE wine and beer section, a world class bakery (we did pay $12.99 for a coffee cake...but oh my! It was the best coffee cake I’ve ever had (sorry Grandma) and fresh baked (not brought in from frozen) bread area so large it’s hard to decide which one to pick.)

text: Not sure if I will be back.  Pros are clean, inviting environment and wide selection including aged prime beef and Iberico ham. I was surprised to see that every food item was handed out in disposable packaging, mostly plastic and none of the eateries offered options for reusable dine-in plates or bowls.  I usually like to buy organic chicken but couldn’t today because of the excessive packaging on it, more like an electronics good than poultry. This location has upgraded their customer service immensely. Staff have been bending over backwards the last couple of times we have been there, always happy to assist. THAT kind of service is what makes me stop shopping at other locations and ONLY shop at the place that won't react with existential dread when I meekly ask for assistance when trying to locate an item.

They also just changed out their entire stock, where things were moved around and new items are now available that weren't previously, but being able to walk a short distance and get actual pomegranate molasses is mind blowing. The produce section is pretty expansive, with items one normally can't locate in a corner grocery store, like massive aloe leaves and mangoes. The majority of the prices are comparable to other local shops, although the quality is definitely higher than say the nearby FL. I have also been able to locate more than just "feta" as a fat free dairy item. That alone was a bonus for me, considering my dietary restrictions. There's the typical salad bar, but the asian cuisine bar was a new one to me. One of those "wait, I can grab orange chicken and fried rice or lo mein for a quick mid-week dinner, without having to pay for delivery? Yes Please!" moments. We got the fried chicken that night with plans to come back for the orange chicken, and we were not disappointed. I added some quickly mixed honey garlic ginger soy sauce over mine, and it was just as tasty as YumYum's korean chicken, at a much more reasonable price point, imo. ($7 vs $24)

The butcher department had 2 people on staff, not the typical overworked solitary person I see at other grocery stores. Which, as a side note, when we went through the store this last time, I kept seeing they had more staff available, even when we got up to the checkout line, and there were TWO people at the checkout assisting us, the cashier and a separate person for bagging, and both were a delight to chat with... which ty again, Addie for going the extra mile to make sure our groceries didn't fall out of the cart!

And ofcourse, the StarBucks on the way out the door. The Barista is a very sweet guy. He may ask a lot of questions, but he is really making sure he is making the EXACT beverage you want, not just thinking he knows what you want... and that means alot to me. Ofcourse, I get being ND, so I appreciate someone who wants to know what I want instead of assuming I meant something else. He asked questions no one else ever has bothered to ask me at a StarBucks, like did I mean the coffee base or dairy base, for the new Pecan drink. I didn't even know there was a dairy base version! I thanked him for asking, because I can't have animal dairy that isn't at least fat-free (preferably denatured, as well - no gallbladder means no raw animal fat, as far as my gastric tract is concerned, particularly for dairy items, otherwise I have to get non-dairy equivalents). Dude literally saved me from days of gastric torment, with that one question. I will absolutely be seeking him out in the future.

All in all, we are in love with this location now. This just became our main grocery store, hands down.

text:
I’ve shopped at this store for years.  I love the selection, produce, meat dept. etc.  I know where everything is….. But, tonight I vowed to never return.

The new self checkout process is a nightmare.  Any extra hand movements you make while putting items in your bags will trigger a “theft” alert, which means you have to wait for a cashier to come clear the alert.

Tonight I had 4 bags of groceries to checkout — approx $200 worth of stuff.

You might wonder why a rational person would go through self-checkout with that much stuff.  Great question!  I didn’t want to, but had little choice.  There were only 2 cashiers in the store, and each of their lines had 4-5 people with completely full carts waiting to check out.  So, off to the self checkout I went.

The new system triggered an “assistant override” 6 times. That means I had to stand there and wait to catch the attention of an HT staff person 6 times before I could leave.  So much for “self checkout.”

This has been my experience the last 3 times I’ve shopped at this store.

I doin’t know if it’s a labor issue, or a deliberate management decision to understaff the “regular” checkout lines so that customers are encouraged to go through self checkout. Regardless of how we got here, the resulting customer experience is abismal.

The last time I shopped at this store, the self checkout showed me a video of myself making “suspicious” movements.  I felt like an accused shoplifter.  As someone who has regularly spent over $200+ per visit — for the last 5-10 years, by the way — I assure you that’s not how a regular customer wants to feel.

So, it was nice while it lasted, Harris Teeter on Tryon Road.  You were my “grocery home” for nearly a decade.

But, now I’m going to Lowes Foods, Wegman’s, Trader Joes, Food Lion, Publix or literally anywhere else in the Raleigh/Cary area.  I’ll drive out of my way to find a store that doesn’t make me feel like an accused criminal while I spend my hard-earned money.

For 3 PLUS years I have been a patron of this location - literally 3 to 4 times every week. There is a Wegmans closer to my home, but I drive out of my way to utilize and support this location!

The presentation of merchandise, store cleanliness (inside and outside), the spirit/energy of the store, great and helpful employees, and quality of products (e.g., produce, meats, seafood, etc.) far exceeded other Wegmans in the area and other grocery stores. I truly did not have to shop anywhere else!

As a result of my frequent visits, I got to know the store manager/Patrick (he noticed I was a repeat shopper): he truly cares about people and honoring the Wegmans Way, as it relates to customers and the service we receive!

Patrick is truly a One-in-a-Million Manager!

I shopped there so much he was known to walk over and say "hello (or can I help you find something)" or  just give me a smile and a "hello" as we passed each other. Hello Mgt Team, have you ever run a decibel study in your Crossroads Store?

Im not a HT frequenter, something I couldn't put my finger on until today (besides I didnt know the optimal spot for tortillas was between the seafood and frozen cakes - who knew?!).... this store is so noisy.

address: 161 Crenshaw Cors Dr, Wake Forest, NC 27587
name: Rita Hedden
text:
Newer Food Lion, that replaced the one on Capital.  It's not as conveniently located for me as the previous one (which had restaurants, a gas station and was close to the pharmacy we use), but its new, which is nice.  It's smaller than previous Food Lion's as well and I noticed that they've really cut down on variety of choice within each category.  Sign of the times, I suppose.  20 years ago you could buy chicken scratch at the old FL; it was a good mix of rural and suburban offerings.  The produce section is completely enclosed and chilled (bring a sweater if you plan to linger), half the stuff that they mist they shouldn't be misting, though.  If I buy loose leaf lettuce there, its a whole process drying it when I get it home so it doesn't rot. They no longer do any real baking in their stores, so that area is smaller.  The staff are usually friendly and pleasant, and very helpful.  The prepared sandwiches and prepared meal offerings are generally good and we like trying new ones every once in a while.

Deli department is kind of useless - dozens of different hams and turkeys but nothing else?  I asked for corned beef and was told they didn't carry it. (???)

My biggest complaint is with the dairy case.  It's disgusting.  Open the door and all you smell is old, not-quite-spoiled milk.  There's drips and spills all over the place and  half the containers appear to be leaking.  I suggested (a few times) that they at least put up a paper towel holder and paper towels; I generally get a disinterested response to that.  I asked a stocker once why it was always like that - he blamed the vendor.  And there's nothing FL can do about that?  I appreciate the cheap milk but Walmart has cheap milk as well and their cases are always clean.  In fact, I don't remember ever seeing such a mess in a dairy case anywhere else.  Is it only this Food Lion?  The staff does not seem interested in addressing this.

One thing I noticed is there is no self-check-out - I think that's a good thing.

The parking lot is small, and awkward and for some reason, only two cart returns are there.  If its cold or hot or raining or snowing (pretty much any and all weather situations in our area) - no one returns their carts.

text:
I am originally from Buffalo, NY, so Wegmans is my hometown grocery store. I have been shopping there for decades and usually have excellent experiences. And, so, it was a major disappointment when I could not get the help that I needed when I visited today.

Recently, a newborn kitten was abandoned on my property. I have limited assistance for help watching her when I run errands, so I often wind up having to take her with me. The staff at Wegmans was friendly and accommodating of my situation on previous visits, but today we were abruptly kicked out of the store. I completely understand having a policy that doesn’t allow animals, and I would not normally bring an animal into the grocery store. However, this kitten is so young that she cannot be left alone, cannot go to the bathroom without stimulation, and is well contained and completely docile. Nevertheless, I can respect the policy. But I cannot respect that, instead of offering a solution to help me (such as checking me out on the app for curbside pickup of my one item – water to make kitten formula with), we were told that we just couldn’t be there. When I took the initiative to inquire about curbside pickup, I was told it could be an option, but when I got back to my car to place the order, there was a minimum 2 hours’ wait before the water could be picked up. It is almost 100 degrees today, and I couldn’t wait that duration in the car without feeding the baby. We wound up going to another store where the staff was more sympathetic and helpful and let me pop in and out for the less than 5 minutes it took to buy water.

I understand rules, but life doesn’t fit into a neat box, and it’s always better to ask someone (who is trying to do the right thing) how you can help before just throwing them out of your store. I still love Wegmans, but I will reconsider shopping at this location while that particular manager is working there.

text:
I go by this store constantly. Usually twice a week or more.

The facility is extremely well maintained. Shelves always stocked. I've yet to go in and the store be missing something I needed. The employees are friendly and helpful, all around great store!

The Asian Bar/Salad bar is fantastic. I do wish the Asian Bar was open a little longer seeing as I don't get off work until 7pm. The options are nice, you have plenty of things to choose from on the Asian Bar. The Salad bar has so many sides to choose from. Boiled eggs, carrots, chicken, and so much more. Good place to stop by and make yourself a salad of your own design.

The Pizza place is great too! You can order a slice or a whole pizza. They have different "Pizza of the Day" everyday, which means that pizza is cheaper than the others. Not to mention Monday you can get the pizza cheaper than any other time of the week, which is fantastic if you want a nice, hot pizza.

I love the Fresh Market. Nothing like getting fresh food to cook for dinner. I went in a little early once, before the Fresh Market opened. The gentleman working the location was kind enough to go ahead and take my order rather than making me wait.

As usually with Harris Teeter, the prices can be a little high, but you're paying for quality. Never disappointed. The fruits and veggies are always fresh, employees always friendly, and store always well maintained.

I'll plan to continue shopping here as long as I live close by!

EDIT: I went up to Harris Teeter the other day wanting a pizza. They advertise that they make pizza until 8pm. We arrive at 740 and there is no one at the pizza counter. Wait a few minutes, someone finally comes over. We ask her if she is still making pizza, she says no. Why advertise that you make pizza until 8, if you're going to close 20 to 30 minutes early?

This place is huge! I've never been to a Wegmans previously, but I've heard lots of good things about it. It seems that they were not exaggerated.

In one side of the store, there were many different areas. There was a food bar, cheese area, fresh seafood, and bread, to name the parts that I remember. From there you can walk to the grocery portion. It's all arranged and looks to have been quite thought through. At the very end of the grocery section, opposite the fresh food area, you can find the alcoholic drinks. It struck me as interesting, since they had a sign that said no sale of alcohol until after 10 am. I've seen these signs in some stores in New Jersey. I wonder if in the weekend they also don't sell certain items? Guess that's something worth exploring at a later visit.

I did get disappointed with the small selection that they had for Asian food and alcoholic beverages. I'm sure that it's an unfair comparison, but I would had thought that certain goodies prevalent in the New York area would also transition to down here. I suppose that was too much to ask.
